Job Description

Join Us as a Pharmacovigilance Coordinator – Make an Impact at the Forefront of Innovation


We have successfully supported the top 50 pharmaceutical companies and more than 750 biotechs, spanning 2,700 clinical trials across 100+ countries in the last 5 years.

As part of our global team, you’ll have the opportunity to provide contracted project coordination and safety support on global and domestic programs. As a Safety Admin, you'll focus on serious and non-serious adverse events, protocol inquiries, physician assessment of diagnostics, Data and Safety Monitoring Boards, and Endpoint Adjudication Committees. In collaboration with Safety Specialists and Medical Monitors, you will liaise and establish effective relationships with internal functional team members to implement projects, prepare contractual documents, coordinate and facilitate meetings, and accurately manage all incoming safety documentation.

What You’ll Do:

  • Coordinates the timely review of protocol inquiries, serious and non-serious adverse events, diagnostics and Data Safety Monitoring Board data; tracks all necessary data and generates reports for the client, project team and/or external vendors.
  • Represents the organization's DSMB/EAC Coordination Team at global and domestic committee meetings (both via teleconference and face-to-face) alongside the client, board members, third party vendors and the project team, coordinating all logistical aspects and assisting with facilitation.
  • Interfaces with various internal and external parties to implement projects, prepares Confidentiality Disclosure Agreements, Letters of Intent and Member Agreements based on contractual considerations; reviewing all contractual documents for accuracy and coordinating internal and external approvals.
  • Compiles adjudication dossiers and creates/submits follow-up to investigative sites.
  • Coordinates/facilitates project meetings, drafts meeting minutes, posts blinded and unblinded minutes/materials to client portals and distributes to internal and external project teams.
  • Manages project specific training and the set-up, maintenance and archival of program files; ensuring PV remains audit ready.
  • Identifies and redacts subject identifiers per local requirements, retrains sites and escalates reoccurrences to the organization's Data Privacy.
  • Performs data entry into internal/external datases, tracking systems and the organization's budget management system; performs system reconciliations to identify issues which may negativley impact project timelines.
  • Oversees expenses and manages translations; ensuring budget parameters are not exceeded.
  • Answers incoming hotline calls, coordinates department functions and performs other duties as assigned.
  • Supports any specific activities performed by the local office, which cannot be performed from elsewhere.
  • Provides training to junior staff.

  • High / Secondary school diploma or equivalent and relevant formal academic / vocational qualification

In some cases an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong problem solving skills
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, demonstrating initative
  • Ability to build strong relationships
  • Ability to effectively analyze project-specific data/systems to ensure accuracy and efficiency
  • Ability to act as a liaison and communicate respectfully and diplomatically with all clients, management, project team members and other internal staff
  • Self-motivated, positive attitude with effective oral and written communication and interpersonal skills
  • Excellent computer skills to include: MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access)
  • Ability to identify and set priorities and effectively perform a variety of tasks simultaneously with strict deadlines
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy with orientation toward careful and meticulous work
  • Ability to maintain a positive and professional demeanor in challenging circumstances

  • Long varied hours required on occasion.

jobs.title: Content Innovation, Claims Editing – Specialty Pharmacy (Multiple Levels)
jobs.description_html:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

About the Opportunity 

Machinify is redefining Payment Integrity through smarter technology, richer data, and intelligent automation. We are seeking a claims editing content expert to help build the next generation of editing content and make healthcare payments more accurate and affordable. This role will bring deep expertise in specialty pharmacy and high-cost drugs.

As Content Innovation, Claims Editing - Specialty Pharmacy you will source, design, validate, and maintain the clinical and coding content that powers our editing products. You will find opportunities in policy and in the data, turn them into edits that hold up, and measure whether they deliver value for our health plan clients. Your focus will be specialty and physician-administered drugs billed under the medical benefit, where you will be our go-to expert on drug coding and payment.

This is a build-and-scale role at the intersection of clinical editing, coding, reimbursement policy, data science, and product development. The ideal candidate brings deep clinical editing and coding expertise, a strong analytical instinct, and an open, practical interest in how AI can help us build better content, faster, while keeping quality and clinical accuracy at the center.

You do not need to be a data scientist. You do need to think in terms of evidence, measurable outcomes, and the value each edit creates for a client.

 

What you’ll do 

Source and author editing content

  • Monitor and interpret authoritative sources, including CPT and HCPCS updates, ICD-10-CM guidelines, NCCI PTP and MUE tables, CMS manuals, NCDs and LCDs, specialty society guidance, and payer reimbursement policies.
  • Translate coding rules, clinical guidelines, and reimbursement policy into precise, testable editing logic.
  • Document the source, rationale, and scope of every edit so it is traceable, defensible on appeal, and easy to maintain.
  • Separate portable, market-wide content from client-specific policy, and flag the difference clearly in all content and sizing work.
  • Maintain existing content through quarterly code updates, policy changes, and performance reviews, and recommend when edits should be refined or retired.

Bring depth in specialty pharmacy and high-cost drugs

  • Monitor and interpret drug content sources, including FDA prescribing information, drug compendia, NCCN and other clinical guidelines, CMS ASP pricing files, NCDs and LCDs, and payer drug policies.
  • Build and maintain edits for HCPCS billing units, NDC-to-HCPCS crosswalks, weight- and BSA-based dosing, maximum units, dose rounding, and drug wastage modifiers such as JW and JZ.
  • Cover oncology, immunology, rare disease, biosimilars, and other high-cost therapeutic areas, including new drug launches and new HCPCS codes.
  • Track label changes, new approvals, quarterly HCPCS updates, and pricing changes, and keep drug content current.

Validate content with data

  • Use claims data to test editing concepts before build, size the opportunity, and estimate hit rate, false-positive rate, and savings.
  • Review edit output and production results to confirm edits fire as intended and to find gaps, over-reach, or missed opportunities.
  • Track measures such as accuracy, hit rate, false positives, appeals, overturns, provider abrasion, and realized savings.
  • Bring an analytical, value-first view to prioritization: what is the opportunity, how confident are we, and what will it return for the client?

Partner with Product and Data Science

  • Work with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to turn content concepts into clear requirements, logic specifications, and test cases.
  • Help data scientists understand clinical and coding context so models and analyses reflect how care is delivered and billed. Bring drug dosing, units, and billing context to that work.
  • Evaluate where AI tools, including large language models, can speed up policy research, concept discovery, content authoring, and quality review.
  • Apply expert judgment to AI-generated content and help define the review standards that keep it accurate.

Support clients and internal teams

  • Explain the rationale, sources, and expected impact behind editing content to client and internal audiences.
  • Support client policy review, edit approval, and appeals with clear, well-sourced documentation.
  • Bring client feedback and operational findings back into the content roadmap.

 

What experience you bring (Role Requirements)  

Required

  • 7+ years of experience in claims editing, clinical coding, Payment Integrity, or payer policy, with hands-on experience authoring or validating edits.
  • Active coding credential, such as CPC, CCS, CCS-P, CPMA, or CIC, or a clinical license (such as RN) paired with deep coding experience.
  • Deep, current knowledge of CPT, HCPCS, ICD-10-CM, modifiers, NCCI, MUEs, coding guidelines, and documentation requirements.
  • Working knowledge of reimbursement methodologies, including fee schedules, DRGs, APCs, and professional and facility billing.
  • Experience sourcing and interpreting primary content, including CMS manuals, NCDs and LCDs, AMA guidance, and payer policies.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with claims data, using SQL, Excel, or similar tools to test hypotheses and measure results.
  • Experience working with Product, Engineering, Data Science, or other multidisciplinary teams.
  • Clear written communication and the ability to explain complex coding and clinical logic to nonclinical audiences.
  • Curiosity about AI tools and willingness to use them in daily content work.
  • At least 3 years of hands-on experience with medical benefit drug billing, coding, or policy, including HCPCS J-codes, NDCs, billing units, drug-related modifiers, and ASP-based reimbursement.
  • Sound judgment and comfort working in a fast-moving build-and-scale environment.

Preferred

  • Pharmacy background, such as PharmD, RPh, or CPhT, or experience in specialty pharmacy, infusion, or oncology practice billing.
  • Experience with 340B billing rules, biosimilar adoption, or oncology drug policy.
  • Experience at a claims editing, Payment Integrity, or healthcare technology company.
  • Experience across commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid lines of business.
  • Clinical background (RN, LPN, or other licensed clinician) with direct patient care experience.
  • Experience writing product requirements or logic specifications for engineering teams.
  • Experience with Python, SQL, or BI tools for claims analysis.
  • Experience presenting content rationale or savings analyses to health plan clients.

 

What Success Looks Like… 

First 90 Days

You will learn Machinify’s content portfolio, source library, technology, and development process; build working relationships with Product and Data Science; assess current drug editing coverage against high-cost therapeutic areas; and deliver a prioritized list of specialty drug content gaps and opportunities.

 Within 6 to 12 months

You will own a content domain end to end, move multiple data-validated concepts into production, maintain accurate and current source documentation, contribute to at least one AI-assisted improvement in how content is built, set up a repeatable process for tracking new approvals, label changes, and HCPCS updates, and show measurable results in edit accuracy, speed, or client value.

 

Pay range: $135,000 - $165,000 USD  

This exempt position. The salary range is for Base Salary. Compensation will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, skill set, years of experience, and the employee’s geographic location. 

 

What’s in it for you       

  • PTO, Paid Holidays, and Volunteer Days
  • Eligibility for health, vision and dental coverage, 401(k) plan participation with company match, and flexible spending accounts
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Eligibility for company-paid benefits including life insurance, short-term disability, and parental leave.
  • Remote and hybrid work options 

 

What values we’ll share with you 

  • Ask why
  • Think big
  • Be humble
  • Optimize for customer impact
  • Deliver results
Equal Employment Opportunity at Machinify
 
We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Machinify is an employment at will employer. We participate in E-Verify as required by applicable law. Who We Are:

SmithRx is a rapidly growing, venture-backed Health-Tech company.  Our mission is to disrupt the expensive and inefficient Pharmacy Benefit Management (PBM) sector by building a next-generation drug acquisition platform driven by cutting edge technology, innovative cost saving tools, and best-in-class customer service.  With hundreds of thousands of members onboarded since 2016, SmithRx has a solution that is resonating with clients all across the country.

We pride ourselves for our mission-driven and collaborative culture that inspires our employees to do their best work. We believe that the U.S healthcare system is in need of transformation, and we come to work each day dedicated to making that change a reality. At our core, we are guided by our company values:

  • Integrity: Our purpose guides our actions and gives us confidence in the path ahead. With unwavering honesty and dependability, we embrace the pressure of challenging the old and exemplify ethical leadership to create the new.
  • Courage: We face continuous challenges with grit and resilience. We embrace the discomfort of the unknown by balancing autonomy with empathy, and ownership with vulnerability. We boldly challenge the status quo to keep moving forward—always.
  • Together: The success of SmithRx reflects the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team. Our shared values bind us together and make us one. When one falls, we all fall; when one rises, we all rise.

Job Summary:

SmithRx is looking for a motivated Senior Clinical Review Operations Pharmacist to serve as a clinical subject matter expert and key operational driver within our Prior Authorization team. This individual contributor role is pivotal in maintaining high-quality clinical reviews, ensuring adherence to turnaround times, and delivering exceptional member experiences. Your primary focus will be building tools to support prior authorization evaluations, driving process improvements, mentoring peer pharmacists on clinical protocols, and serving as a key cross-functional innovator  to scale our clinical operations.

What you will do:

  • Process & Technology Optimization: Identify operational process gaps and champion technology-driven solutions to improve throughput, scalability, and workflow efficiency.
  • Clinical Mentorship & Quality Assurance: Serve as a clinical peer lead, providing guidance, coaching, and onboarding support to fellow pharmacists to foster clinical consistency and quality.
  • Complex Escalations: Act as a senior operational contact for complex clinical cases, escalated coverage determinations, and appeals.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with internal teams to troubleshoot eligibility questions, claims adjudication, and benefit design nuances.
  • Clinical Policy & P&T Committee Support: Collaborate with clinical leadership and the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee to help develop, refine, and review clinical criteria for medications requiring prior authorization.
  • Performance & SLAs: Consistently meet or exceed individual target KPIs and turn-around-time (TAT) SLAs to maintain seamless operating standards.
  • Change Champion: Drive adoption of new technology, workflow tools, and updated clinical protocols across the Clinical Review team.

What you will bring to SmithRx:

  • 5+ years of health plan or Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) experience, specifically involved in prior authorization review and clinical operations.
  • Demonstrated expertise as a clinical subject matter expert with a track record of driving process improvements or technology-driven efficiencies.
  • Active Pharmacist License (unrestricted) required.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Pharmacy or Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) required.
  • Strong proficiency with Mac, MS Office, and G-Suite platforms.
  • High degree of empathy with excellent active listening and communication skills to clearly convey complex clinical information to members, providers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Proven self-starter with superior multitasking, time management, and problem-solving abilities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Deep understanding of drug product/dose calculations, claim adjudication rules, and general pharmacy dispensing processes.
  • Adaptability to evolving clinical guidelines, changing protocols, and new operational technology.

Education and Experience:

  • At least Bachelors’ degree (or country equivalent) in computer science, data science, computational linguistics, applied statistics/biostatistics, life sciences / Information technology or other relevant field required.
  • Python, ML/NLP frameworks, model deployment/monitoring, MLOps tooling, ideally exposure to LLMs on unstructured clinical/safety text.
  • Familiarity with, or ability to rapidly acquire, GVP/21 CFR 314 concepts preferred
  • working understanding of safety database data models (Argus/ArisG) and E2B(R3) structure.
  • Relevant experience in IT / Safety / Clinical Research / Pharmacovigilance overall with at least 3 years of proven experience with safety database systems (e.g. ARGUS or ArisG) including workflow management
  • Equivalent and adequate combination of education and experience or proven practical expertise in all of the required skills

In some cases, an equivalency, consisting of a combination of appropriate education, training and/or directly related experience, will be considered sufficient for an individual to meet the requirements of the role

Knowledge, Skills, and Responsibilities:

  • Proficiency in Python for ML development, including scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy; experience with at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch or TensorFlow).
  • Natural language processing for extraction of adverse events, drugs, and outcomes from unstructured text - case narratives, medical literature, call transcripts, and spontaneous reports.
  • Named Entity Recognition (NER), relation extraction, and text classification
  • Experience with transformer-based / large language models (BERT-family, clinical/biomedical models such as BioBERT or PubMedBERT, and modern LLMs) for narrative generation, summarization, and information extraction.
  • MedDRA and WHODrug auto-coding using ML/NLP; prompt engineering and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) a plus.
  • Supervised and unsupervised methods for classification, clustering, and anomaly detection.
  • Feature engineering and model evaluation (precision/recall trade-offs, ROC/AUC, calibration) with an understanding of why recall and sensitivity are weighted heavily in a safety context.
  • Model lifecycle management: versioning, monitoring, drift detection, retraining pipelines using standard MLOps tooling (e.g. MLflow, Azure ML, Databricks) in line with client DT/BIS standards
  • Model explainability / interpretability (SHAP, LIME) - essential where decisions must be defensible to health authorities.
  • Understanding of GxP / GAMP 5 validation as applied to AI/ML systems, model governance, and emerging regulatory expectations (EMA reflection paper on AI, FDA guidance) — rare and worth flagging as preferred.
  • Proficiency in Safety Database systems (e.g. Argus) and knowledge of other technical systems applicable to Safety /Pharmacovigilance (e.g. E2B gateway, safety signal detection tools and systems) is a plus.
  • Proficiency in electronic systems commonly used for Safety / PV, like for data visualization and analysis, dashboards
  • Solid understanding of the quality management processes, metrics and KPIs
  • Good knowledge of relevant pharmacovigilance regulatory requirements and guidance documents (including Europe, US, Japan)
  • Proficient in the Microsoft 365 stack (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive) and in modern collaboration and documentation tooling
  • Advanced Excel required; working proficiency in SQL required for querying safety and operational datasets
  • Ability to communicate effectively and collaborate successfully across functions and with vendors
  • Fluent communication in written and spoken English required
  • Ability to work independently with minimal oversight and prioritize effectively
  • Ability to complete multiple complex deliverables within tight timelines
  • Ability to function effectively in a team environment

Working Environment:
Thermo Fisher Scientific values the health and wellbeing of our employees. We support and encourage individuals to create a healthy and balanced environment where they can thrive.

jobs.title: Pharmacy Development Coordinator
jobs.description_html:
Company Overview:

Strive Pharmacy is a personalized compounding pharmacy built on a simple conviction: medicine should fit the patient, not the other way around. We started Strive because we believed the pharmaceutical industry was overdue for a more human approach—one that prioritizes individualized care, clinical nuance, and genuine partnership with patients and providers.

Compounding gives us the tools to do that. Every formulation we prepare is built to the specific needs of a specific person, and every interaction we have is guided by that same commitment to personalized care.

We're growing, and we're looking for people who share that conviction. If you're ready to be part of a pharmacy that takes the work seriously and the people even more seriously, we'd like to meet you.

Mission:

Strive exists to disrupt an industry long overdue for a more personal approach to care. We put the human element at the center of everything: every formulation, every patient interaction, every provider partnership. We're not just a compounding pharmacy. We're a team on a mission to change what personalized healthcare looks and feels like.

Position Type: Full-time

Location: Remote with frequent travel to active project and build-out sites nationwide (central time zone preferred).

Position Overview:

The Pharmacy Development Coordinator takes the strategic direction set by the Director of Pharmacy Development and turns it into action: initiating, aligning, executing, and maintaining the projects and programs that keep Strive's sites running and growing. This includes new construction and build-outs, environmental monitoring, security, asset management, breakroom management, lease and real estate management, vendor management, and other department programs as assigned. This role owns the day-to-day work of bringing these programs to life and keeping them running well long after launch: coordinating with vendors and internal teams, keeping details from slipping, providing on-site support where needed, and sustaining programs through renewals, monitoring, and troubleshooting. The ideal candidate is highly organized, a strong communicator, and energized by follow-through. Travel is required.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Take direction from the Director of Pharmacy Development and turn department strategy into executed action across assigned projects and programs.
  • Initiate, align, and execute construction and build-out projects, coordinating with vendors, contractors, and internal teams, and providing on-site support as needed.
  • Own the implementation of programs handed off by the Director, such as security, environmental monitoring, asset management, break-room management, and lease and real estate management.
  • Sustain programs once implemented: track recurring tasks and renewals, monitor vendor performance, keep documentation current, and flag issues before they become problems.
  • Coordinate vendor communications, including scheduling, deliverable tracking, and follow-up, escalating concerns to the Director.
  • Maintain department documentation and standard operating procedures so programs stay consistent across sites.

Required Qualifications:

  • 1 - 3+ years of experience supporting or owning multi-stakeholder projects or recurring operational programs is preferred; multi-site, construction, or facilities exposure is a plus.
  • Experience managing programs with recurring deadlines (contract or lease renewals, compliance-driven maintenance schedules, recurring vendor deliverables), and comfort sustaining a program, not just launching it.
  • Exposure to one or more of: construction/build-outs, physical security systems, environmental monitoring, asset tracking, or lease/real estate administration.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent work streams.
  • Comfortable working directly with vendors, contractors, and on-site teams, and knowing when to escalate.
  • Pharmacy, healthcare, or other regulated-environment experience is a plus, including familiarity with environmental monitoring requirements relevant to pharmacy operations.
  • Proficiency with project and work management tools; Asana experience preferred

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Background in facilities management, physical security systems, or lease/real estate administration.
  • Experience supporting programs across multiple site types (retail, healthcare, or other multi-location operations).

Work Environment:

This position is primarily based in a remote work environment and requires regular computer use, sitting, and standing, with occasional lifting as needed. Regular travel (30%) may be required for implementations, site visits and audits. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with disabilities.

Annual Salary
$60,000—$80,000 USD

Join Us in Making an Impact:

At Strive, the work is real and the impact is direct. Every role here contributes to a patient experience that's more personal, more attentive, and more human than what most people have come to expect from a pharmacy. Apply today and help us raise the bar.

Benefits/ Perks:

Strive Pharmacy offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Employer-paid healthcare coverage, effective the 1st day of the following month of your hire date
  • Free Strive compounded medications for employees based on a valid patient-specific prescription from a licensed healthcare provider
  • Paid time off
  • Sick time
  • FSA and HSA options
  • Parental leave
  • 401(k) with employer matching
  • Life insurance
  • Vision and dental insurance
  • Veterinary insurance

Culture:

Culture isn't an afterthought at Strive. It's something we actively build. We foster a collaborative, engaging workplace where employees have opportunities to connect, celebrate, and build meaningful relationships with their colleagues. We're committed to supporting the personal and professional growth of every employee, both inside and outside the workplace.

Job Summary:

The Pharmacy Network Contracting Manager supports the Director of Contracting by serving as the principal process owner for  day-to-day pharmacy network contracting operations while partnering closely with Provider Relations to support a strong provider experience at scale. Operating as a highly autonomous individual contributor, this role owns the contracting pipeline and governance, and ensures agreements are negotiated, executed, and accurately configured in SmithRx’s claims adjudication system—including reimbursement rates, network participation, and effective dates. The key objective is to improve contracting throughput, consistency, configuration accuracy, and audit readiness while reducing provider friction through clear coordination, communication, and issue resolution.

What you will do:

  • Lead day-to-day pharmacy contracting operations, serving as the principal subject matter expert and providing mentorship and process guidance to team members.
  • Own and optimize the contracting pipeline (intake, prioritization, aging, execution timelines, and deliverables).
  • Govern  the end-to-end contract lifecycle across new agreements, amendments, renewals, notices, and terminations, including milestone and deadline tracking.
  • Lead complex contract negotiation workflows and redline reviews partnering directly with Legal and internal stakeholders to mitigate systemic risks.
  • Ensure all reimbursement exhibits, fee schedules, and effective dates are meticulously accurate, approved, and implementation-ready.
  • Drive rate loading and network configuration in the claims adjudication system to ensure executed terms are implemented accurately and on time.
  • Architect and enforce controls and QA frameworks for rate setup (effective dates, plan/network mapping, reimbursement logic, and exception handling).
  • Monitor and manage the rate load/configuration backlog, proactively prioritize urgent builds, mitigate and escalate risks that could impact go-lives or claim outcomes.
  • Own post-load validation checkpoints (test claims/spot checks, variance reviews, and issue triage) lead root-cause analysis and ensure corrections are completed.
  • Partner strategically with Provider Relations to align contracting timelines, onboarding requirements, and provider-facing communications during contracting and execution.
  • Act as the definitive escalation point for contracting- or configuration-related provider escalations; document root causes and drive resolution through and across the appropriate teams.
  • Author, govern, and maintain contracting playbooks, SOPs, templates, clause guidance, and standard responses to improve speed, consistency, and provider clarity.
  • Drive contract repository and configuration documentation governance (version control, naming standards, executed package completeness, approvals, and change history).
  • Leverage data to provide routine reporting on contracting/configuration volume, cycle time, backlog, and issue trends; lead continuous process improvement initiatives to scale operations.
  • Architect and maintain a comprehensive contracting knowledge base (FAQs, standard workflows, and escalation paths) to drive internal enablement and elevate the provider experience.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience in PBM, managed care, healthcare contracting, network operations, or provider relations.
  • 8+ years of experience in pharmacy/provider contracting, PBM network operations, or healthcare contract administration.
  • 2+ years of experience serving as a principal subject matter expert, process owner and/or managing high-volume contracting workflows.
  • Exceptional ability to interpret complex contract language, lead redline negotiations, and strategically identify business, operational, and compliance risks.
  • Deep technical understanding  of claims adjudication and pharmacy reimbursement configuration (how executed terms translate into system setup).
  • Proven experience architecting or overseeing rate loading and configuration accuracy, including effective-date controls and mapping requirements.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist - Care Team
jobs.description_html:
ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Clinical Pharmacist, Care Team is a member of the Rightway PBM Clinical Operations team. This role will be key in delivering on the “pharmacist in the family” approach to engaging our members. We are looking for an experienced clinical pharmacist to engage with our members in a caring and empathetic manner. Written and verbal communication skills will be critical when interacting with members on the phone, via email, and via the chat function on the Rightway app. A willingness to go the extra mile to provide outstanding customer service is an essential requirement of this role.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Guide members as if you are the “Pharmacist in the Family” to help members manage their medications and disease states
  • Engage with members via phone, chat, and email to provide a white glove/concierge experience for members
  • Go above and beyond to answer member questions about all things pharmacy related
  • Perform core Pharmacist duties including prospective/retrospective drug utilization reviews, comprehensive medication reviews, and recommending changes to patient's drug regimens
  • Partners with Rightway’s Navigation team where needed to provide holistic support to members
  • Engages with providers to address medication gaps in therapy for patients, drug therapy recommendations, formulary compliance, and serve as a subject matter expert on medications
  • Contributes to the Pharmacy & Therapeutics committee in the research, preparation and presentation of drug monographs, therapeutic category reviews and clinical policy development.  Ensures that these processes meet or exceed regulatory and best practice standards
  • Supports prior authorization review process as needed regarding drug product selection and formulary compliance to ensure quality of care
  • Perform utilization management reviews and support outreach to members and providers to drive clinical and cost-savings outcomes.
  • Effectively collaborate with third-parties in the administration of Rightway’s clinical pharmacy strategy
  • Responsible for achieving productivity and quality of work metrics for clinical pharmacy interactions
  • Contribute to the design and evolution of technology-enabled processes to create a scalable clinical pharmacy operation
  • Ensures regulatory standards are consistently met

WHO YOU ARE:

  • Pharmacy degree required, PharmD preferred. Managed Care or other pharmacy residency preferred
  • 3 years in direct patient care such as PBM clinical operations or Health Plan Pharmacy Department or provision of Medication Therapy Management services
  • Pharmacy License: Required: State of residence. Preferred: Multi-state licenses and/or be willing to attain licensure in additional states
  • Empathetic, detail-oriented, intellectually and clinically curious, good listener, ability to challenge status quo, values exemplar
  • Great clinician, effective & creative problem-solver, ability to prioritize and manage through change. Solid communication skills, ability to lead projects and influence others even without direct reporting line ownership
  • Occasional travel may be required

COMPENSATION:  $120,000 - $125,000 annually, in addition to bonus and equity.

Compensation offered will be determined by geographic location, experience, and qualifications.

CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS NOTICE

In response to ongoing and industry-wide fraudulent recruitment activities (i.e., job scams), Rightway wants to inform potential candidates that we will only contact them from the @rightwayhealthcare.com email domain. We will never ask for bank details or deposits of any kind as a condition of employment. 

ABOUT RIGHTWAY:

Rightway is on a mission to harmonize healthcare for everyone, everywhere. Our products guide patients to the best care and medications by inserting clinicians and pharmacists into a patient’s care journey through a modern, mobile app. Rightway is a front door to healthcare, giving patients the tools they need along with on-demand access to Rightway health guides, human experts that answer their questions and manage the frustrating parts of healthcare for them.

Since its founding in 2017, Rightway has raised over $300mm from investors including Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, Francisco Partners, and Tiger Global. We’re headquartered in New York City, with satellite offices in Denver and Dallas. Our clients rely on us to transform the healthcare experience, improve outcomes for their teams, and decrease their healthcare costs.

HOW WE LIVE OUR VALUES TO OUR TEAMMATES:

We’re seeking those with passion for healthcare and relentless devotion to our goal. We need team members that embody our core values:

1) We are human, first
Our humanity binds us together. We bring the same empathetic approach to every individual we engage with, whether it be our members, our clients, or each other. We are all worthy of respect and understanding and we engage in our interactions with care and intention. We honor our stories. We listen to—and hear—each other, we celebrate our differences and similarities, we are present for each other, and we strive for mutual understanding.

2) We redefine what is possible
We always look beyond the obstacles in front of us to imagine new solutions. We approach our work with inspiration from other industries, other leaders, and other challenges. We use ingenuity and resourcefulness when faced with tough problems.

3) We debate then commit
We believe that a spirit of open discourse is part of a healthy culture. We understand and appreciate different perspectives and we challenge our assumptions. When working toward a decision or a new solution, we actively listen to one another, approach it with a “yes, and” mentality, and assume positive intent. Once a decision is made, we align and champion it as one team.

4) We cultivate grit
Changing healthcare doesn’t happen overnight. We reflect and learn from challenges and approach the future with a determination to strive for better. In the face of daunting situations, we value persistence. We embrace failure as a stepping stone to future success. On this journey, we seek to act with guts, resilience, initiative, and tenacity.

5) We seek to delight
Healthcare is complicated and personal. We work tirelessly to meet the goals of our clients while also delivering the best experience to our members. We recognize that no matter the role or team, we each play a crucial part in our members’ care and take that responsibility seriously. When faced with an obstacle, we are kind, respectful, and solution-oriented in our approach. We hold ourselves accountable to our clients and our members’ success.

Rightway is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes in the strength of diverse thought, beliefs, backgrounds, and education. We foster an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated to drive the best business decisions possible. We do not discriminate on any basis protected by applicable law. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, need, and performance.

Job Description
The Associate Director of Service Operations is responsible for building, launching, and leading the patient and provider service operation for the pharmacy hub. This leader owns the quality, timeliness, and consistency of inbound and outbound service across phone and digital channels, including patient support, provider support, case follow-up, status communications, refill and program coordination, service recovery, and complex issue resolution.

As a launch leader, the Associate Director will establish the service operating model, workforce practices, interaction standards, escalation pathways, and performance routines required to deliver a differentiated experience. The role partners closely with Access Operations, Clinical Operations, Implementation, Workforce Management, Quality, Training, Product, Technology, Analytics, Client Services, and external vendors.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience leading healthcare contact center, patient services, provider services, hub, PBM, specialty pharmacy, or other regulated service operations. Success requires strong omnichannel service leadership, disciplined workforce and performance management, and the ability to balance patient experience, client commitments, compliance, and cost to serve.

Key Responsibilities

Launch, Service Model & Readiness

  • Build the Service Operations model, including channels, hours of operation, staffing structure, interaction types, call flows, queue design, escalation paths, and service standards.
  • Partner with Implementation on requirements, workflow validation, user acceptance testing, training readiness, cutover, go-live, and hypercare; assume steady-state accountability after formal acceptance.
  • Translate patient, provider, client, and program needs into scripts, interaction guidance, knowledge content, routing, and measurable service expectations.
  • Establish launch staffing, nesting, proficiency, contingency, and escalation plans aligned to volume forecasts and program complexity.

Patient & Provider Service Performance

  • Lead patient and provider support across voice and digital channels, case follow-up, program education, refill coordination, status updates, outbound outreach, and service recovery.
  • Own service level, speed to answer, abandonment, responsiveness, first-contact resolution, transfer rate, repeat contacts, quality, satisfaction, and complaint outcomes.
  • Implement daily operating routines for real-time management, queue balancing, schedule adherence, backlog control, escalations, and recovery planning.
  • Use interaction and journey data to reduce effort, prevent avoidable contacts, improve resolution, and strengthen patient and provider trust.

Workforce, Quality & Coaching

  • Recruit, develop, and retain managers, supervisors, team leads, service specialists, and resolution specialists as the organization scales.
  • Partner with Workforce Management on forecasting, staffing, scheduling, shrinkage, intraday management, overtime, and capacity scenarios.
  • Establish interaction quality standards, calibration, coaching, nesting, knowledge reinforcement, and performance accountability.
  • Build a service culture that combines empathy, accuracy, ownership, compliance, and timely escalation.

Experience, Complaints & Resolution

  • Establish clear complaint, grievance, escalation, service recovery, and executive case pathways with defined ownership and documentation standards.
  • Monitor contact drivers, repeat contacts, transfer patterns, escalations, sentiment signals, and failure demand to identify systemic improvements.
  • Coordinate complex resolutions across Access, Clinical, fulfillment, vendors, technology, and client teams.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Pharmacy Hub Operations
jobs.description_html:
Become a part of our caring community
 

The Associate Director of Pharmacy Hub Operations is responsible for helping build, launch, and lead the pharmacy hub operating model across patient access and clinical services. During launch, this leader will provide broad operational oversight across the end-to-end model, including intake and enrollment, benefits verification, prior authorization support, appeals coordination, financial assistance navigation, complex access issue resolution, and the initial pharmacist, nurse, and pharmacy technician service capabilities.

The position is intentionally designed for a versatile operations leader who can establish integrated workflows, staffing, readiness, quality controls, escalation pathways, and performance routines across the launch organization. As the hub scales and dedicated leadership structures are established, the role may evolve to lead Access Operations, Clinical Operations, or another major area of Pharmacy Hub Operations based on the leader’s experience and strengths, organizational needs, program mix, operating complexity, and business growth. The role partners closely with Implementation, Service Operations, the Pharmacist-in-Charge, Product, Technology, Quality, Compliance, Workforce Management, Training, Analytics, and external vendors.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in manufacturer hub services, specialty pharmacy, patient access, reimbursement support, clinical services, or pharmacy operations and demonstrates the range to lead across multiple operational disciplines. Success requires hands-on launch leadership, disciplined performance management, strong judgment in a regulated environment, and the ability to build scalable teams while adapting leadership scope as the organization matures.

Key Responsibilities

Launch, Operating Model & Readiness

  • Build the launch operating model across Access Operations and initial Clinical Operations, including team structure, role clarity, workflows, queue design, escalation paths, controls, and performance routines.
  • Establish integrated launch workflows across access specialists, resolution resources, pharmacists, nurses, and pharmacy technicians, including role boundaries, handoffs, coverage, escalation, and governance.
  • Partner with Implementation on requirements, workflow validation, user acceptance testing, training readiness, cutover, go-live, and hypercare; assume operational accountability following formal acceptance.
  • Translate manufacturer requirements, business rules, clinical protocols, service-level commitments, scope-of-practice requirements, and compliance obligations into executable practices.
  • Establish launch staffing, hiring sequences, licensing and credentialing dependencies, onboarding expectations, and contingency plans.

Access Operations Leadership

  • Lead intake and enrollment, benefits verification, prior authorization support, appeals coordination, copay and patient assistance navigation, and access-related case resolution.
  • Own service-level attainment, turnaround time, backlog, aging, productivity, quality, rework, abandonment, and end-to-end access outcomes.
  • Implement daily management routines, capacity controls, queue balancing, escalation management, and recovery plans.
  • Use operational data to reduce time to therapy, avoidable touches, access delays, and case leakage.

Clinical Operations Launch Oversight

  • Provide operational oversight for clinical review, patient education, adherence and persistence support, therapy-specific outreach, care coordination, and technician-supported workflows during launch.
  • Partner with the Pharmacist-in-Charge and clinical, quality, compliance, legal, and medical leaders on pharmacy policies, patient safety, clinical escalation, adverse-event and product-complaint pathways, and regulatory accountability.
  • Ensure pharmacist, nurse, and pharmacy technician activities have appropriate licensure, credentialing, competency, supervision, documentation, and scope-of-practice controls.
  • Establish clinical workload, quality, documentation, intervention, escalation, and patient-safety measures for launch and early ramp.
  • Support the future-state organizational design and leadership transition as volume, program mix, complexity, and regulatory needs increase; be prepared to assume ongoing leadership of Access Operations, Clinical Operations, or another major hub operating area based on business need and individual fit.

People, Workforce & Quality Leadership

  • Recruit, develop, coach, and retain leaders and frontline resources across access and launch-phase clinical services, while building succession and transition plans for the future-state organization.
  • Set productivity, quality, and competency expectations by work type and discipline; establish calibration, coaching, and performance-management routines.
  • Partner with Workforce Management on staffing, scheduling, shrinkage, overtime, licensed coverage, and capacity plans.
  • Partner with Quality and Compliance on monitoring, audit readiness, corrective actions, complaint trends, clinical incidents, and control effectiveness.

Cross-Functional & Client Partnership

  • Represent the integrated Pharmacy Hub Operations model in launch governance, performance reviews, client discussions, and decision forums.
  • Coordinate handoffs across Access Operations, Clinical Operations, Service Operations, pharmacy fulfillment, external vendors, and provider-facing teams as the model matures.
  • Partner with Product and Technology on automation, rules configuration, clinical decision support, reporting, AI enablement, and user-experience improvements.
  • Provide executive updates on readiness, capacity, performance, patient safety, risks, transition triggers, and recovery actions.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations & Compliance
jobs.description_html:
Vera Therapeutics is a commercial-stage biotechnology company focused on the pursuit of truth in science to transform medicine in autoimmune disease, starting with the kidney. Vera Therapeutics’ flagship commercial product is TRUTAKNATM (atacicept-vymj), a B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) inhibitor. Vera Therapeutics is evaluating multiple diseases where the reduction of autoantibodies through inhibition of BAFF and APRIL may prove clinically meaningful. Vera Therapeutics was founded in 2016 and is based in Brisbane, California. To learn more, visit www.veratx.com.
 
At Vera, our values are the cornerstone of our culture and guide how we work together every day. We lead with empathy, act with an owner’s mindset, demand clarity, work without fences, and execute with urgency because patients are counting on us. From how we hire and develop our people to how we advance rigorous science, we are building a team committed to transforming medicine in autoimmune diseases, starting with the kidney. 

Position Summary:

This position is responsible for creating, directing, and managing the company’s infrastructure and staff to support the operational aspects of the pharmacovigilance operations and compliance system to adhere to all global regulatory requirements and internal processes and procedures. The qualified candidate will have experience in and perform multiple activities related to overall safety operations strategy across the portfolio, including oversight of case management, database strategy, vendor oversight, compliance, inspection readiness, contracts, departmental strategy and training. In addition, this position must build and maintain relationships with key strategic internal and external stakeholders, including the hiring and development of Drug Safety and Pharmacovigilance (DSPV) personnel. As a member of the DSPV leadership team, this role partners closely with the Head of DSPV to shape PV Operations strategy, own budget and resourcing decisions, and represent DSPV Operations to senior leadership and external partners.

Responsibilities:
  • Own and drive global PV Operations strategy, including planning, implementation, and management, in the US and globally internationally, in close alignment with the Head of DSPV on portfolio-level risk, resourcing, and business priorities.
  • Serve as a key advisor to the Head of DSPV on operational risk, resource allocation, and DSPV budget planning; own accountability for the DSPV Operations budget, including CRO and vendor contract spend.
  • Represent DSPV Operations in interactions with senior leadership and, as needed, and support due diligence activities (e.g., licensing, partnerships, M&A).
  • Manage internal and external staff allocated to operational PV activities, creating a highly efficient team.
  • Own talent strategy for PV Operations, including hiring, development, performance management, and succession planning.
  • Provide expert guidance and leadership both internally and externally based on in-depth knowledge of development and post-marketing safety requirements, per ICH, US and international regulations and guidelines, and Good Pharmacovigilance Practice.
  • Build and implement pharmacovigilance systems that are fully compliant with the applicable worldwide Health Authority PV regulations.
  • Provide oversight of systems and MedDRA updates in collaboration with the relevant PV vendor.
  • Contribute to the selection of PV vendors to support an outsourced PV business model. Provide vendor oversight and management for all outsourced or insourced PV activities, including establishing and monitoring key quality and compliance metrics, invoicing and budgetary needs related to operations and compliance.
  • Develop and implement an inspection readiness program with the contribution of other PV and non-PV stakeholders.
  • Serve as the PV Operations lead/host during Health Authority inspections and audits (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA), coordinating responses and remediation.
  • Responsible for a compliant and quality execution of all operational activities related to case management and related activities. Oversee timely submissions of expedited reports to the FDA and other health authorities in conjunction with Regulatory.
  • Establish a system for identifying, preventing, and correcting compliance deviation, including applicable corrective and preventive actions, in collaboration with the Quality group and internal/external stakeholders, to maintain reporting compliance at the highest level.
  • Oversee the setup of new safety projects, including development of study-specific Safety Management Plans and setup of safety systems and database configurations in the PV database to accommodate these trials and products.
  • Contribute to, draft, and implement department SOPs and work instructions related to the PV activities.
  • Contribute to the signal detection, benefit-risk profile assessment, and aggregate reporting activities with providing accurate reports from the safety database.
  • Effectively collaborate with key stakeholders at all levels in the organization, including Clinical Operations, Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, Medical Affairs, and Manufacturing to develop compliant procedures in line with industry standards and best practices.
  • Represent PV Operations as a leader on project teams, cross-functional committees, and governance bodies (e.g., Safety Management Team), providing operational input to signal review and safety governance processes.
  • Elevate a quality mindset across DSPV.
  • Lead training activities, including setting training requirements and training compliance.
  • Build and oversee PV regulatory intelligence activities.

 

Qualifications:
  • Healthcare or life sciences degree required; advanced degree (e.g., PharmD, RN, MPH, or scientific PhD) preferred.
  • 15+ years of pharmacovigilance experience, including 5+ years in a people-leadership role managing global PV teams.
  • Experience with clinical and commercial lifecycle phases is required.
  • Demonstrated experience managing PV Operations through multiple Health Authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA).
  • Experience spanning both clinical-stage and commercial/post-marketing environments, ideally across multiple therapeutic areas.
  • Skilled in process gap assessments and process enhancements.
  • Strategic thinker.
  • Strong execution and drive for results skills.
  • Comfortable working independently.
  • Deep knowledge of pharmacovigilance regulations and guidelines.

Vera Therapeutics Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer.

Vera Therapeutics is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices and we strive to provide employees with total compensation packages that are market competitive. The exact base pay offered for this role will depend on various factors, including but not limited to the candidate’s geography, qualifications, skills, and experience.

For this role, the anticipated base pay range is
$270,000—$370,000 USD

At Vera, base pay is only one part of your total compensation package. The successful candidate will be eligible for an annual performance incentive bonus, new hire equity, and ongoing performance-based equity. Vera Therapeutics also offers various benefits offerings, including, but not limited to, medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401k match, flexible time off, and a number of paid holidays.

Recruiters and staffing agencies should not contact Vera Therapeutics through this page. All recruitment vendors (search firms, recruitment agencies, and staffing companies) are prohibited from contacting our hiring manager(s), executive team members, or employees.

1. Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business Management, or Hospital Administration 

2. Nationally Certified Pharmacy Technician

3. Apexus Advanced 340B Operations Certificate

EXPERIENCE:

1. 340B Drug Pricing Program experience.

2. Experience in data analysis, audit process and reporting.

3. Hospital or retail pharmacy experience.

2. Reviews and monitors utilization records and 340B purchasing accounts to ensure software or tools are working properly and accurately, performing audits or compliance assessments to validate processes.

3. Monitors monthly and annual reports on 340B Program participation which clearly documents utilization, savings, problem areas and exceptions or discrepancies.

4. Performs monthly compliance audits of contract pharmacies, hospital owned retail pharmacies, specialty pharmacies and hospital mixed use pharmacy to ensure that all 340B HRSA regulations are upheld.

5. Performs monthly compliance audits of patient eligibility, provider eligibility, and location eligibility.

6. Monitors purchasing records where 340B participation occurs, clearly documenting utilization, savings, problem areas and exceptions or discrepancies, to be shared with pharmacy leadership, Finance and Administration.

7. Maintains 340B Program software to ensure appropriate products are mapped to the appropriate charge code and in the correct ratio as well as maintain system when new charge codes are created.

jobs.description_html:
AnewHealth is one of the nation’s leading pharmacy care management companies that specializes in caring for people with the most complex, chronic needs—wherever they call home. We enable better outcomes for patients and the healthcare organizations who support them. Established in 2023 through the combination of ExactCare and Tabula Rasa HealthCare, we provide a suite of solutions that includes comprehensive pharmacy services; full-service pharmacy benefit management; and specialized support services for Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. With over 1,400 team members, we care for more than 100,000 people across all 50 states.

Job Details


Under the direction of the Director or Manager the Pharmacy Technician will bridge the service gap needed to provide service support to PACE clients and their participants in facilities along with the network pharmacies servicing them.  

 

Responsibilities


  • Receives electronic prescriptions, weekly batches or refill requests and accurately and efficiently fills the prescriptions under the direction of the Pharmacist. Performs pharmacy tasks such as handling, counting, mixing, and packaging medications. 
  • Assists in entering minor edits to record correct dispensing quantity and manufacturer NDC used to dispense prescription order. 
  • Performs reclamation duties. 
  • Uses pharmacy software to check and/record data about prescriptions. 
  • Acts as a liaison between our customers and their providers and our pharmacy, receives and triages incoming phone calls and messages to answer questions, fill prescription orders or handle other requests to ensure that clients have a positive experience. 
  • Establishes and maintains patient profiles, including lists of medications taken by individual patients, and uses our advanced proprietary software system to document medication care plans. 
  • Uses pharmaceutical technician expertise to ensure compliance, efficiency, and quality of operations. Participates in company quality initiatives, recognizing opportunities for improvements and reporting quality assurance issues.
  • Secures information in accordance with the privacy and security guidelines of the Company and applicable regulations such as HIPAA. 
  • Provides enrollment support for new PACE enrollees.
  • Communicates pharmacy benefit information to network pharmacies contracted with facilities where CK PACE participants reside.
  • Coordinate facility discharges to assure medication reconciliation is complete and delivery to home is back in place.
  • Provides help desk support to network pharmacies.
  • Education PACE staff regarding CK and network pharmacy processes for facility participants.
  • Makes outgoing calls to gather/confirm information necessary to process customer requests or otherwise contribute to pharmacy operations.
  • Coordinates and sets up couriers to ensure timely medication delivery.
  • Makes outgoing calls to ensure the participants have received their delivery.

 

The above essential functions are representative of major duties of positions in this job classification. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs. Other duties may be assigned similar to the above consistent with knowledge, skills and abilities required for the job.  Not all of the duties may be assigned to a position. 

 

Qualifications  


  • Possesses high level of integrity 
  • Quality-oriented 
  • Innovative 
  • Steadfast 

Education


  • Required: HS diploma required.

jobs.title: Director / Senior Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations
jobs.description_html:
Rezolute is a late-stage rare disease biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative therapies for patients living with severe metabolic and endocrine disorders. Our mission is to bring hope and meaningful solutions to patients and families affected by rare and difficult-to-treat diseases through scientific innovation, collaboration, and integrity.

Rezolute’s lead investigational therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is a fully human monoclonal antibody in late-stage clinical development for the treatment of hypoglycemia due to congenital and acquired forms of hyperinsulinism (HI). As Rezolute expands its medical and scientific focus into tumor-related hyperinsulinism (tumor HI), most commonly related to pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (insulinomas) or paraneoplastic hypoglycemia (NICTH), the company is committed to advancing novel therapeutic strategies that address this rare and complex form of hypoglycemia associated with insulin-secreting tumors and related neuro-oncology disorders

More information can be found at rezolutebio.com

 

The Director / Senior Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations will play a critical leadership role in building and executing the company’s pharmacovigilance and drug safety capabilities as the organization advances its lead product toward regulatory approval and commercial launch.

This individual will be responsible for ensuring an effective, scalable, and inspection-ready pharmacovigilance system supporting late-stage clinical development, regulatory submissions, product launch, and post-marketing safety surveillance. The role will provide leadership across safety operations, benefit-risk management, signal detection and management, aggregate reporting, safety governance, vendor oversight, and global regulatory compliance.

As the company evolves from a development-stage organization to a commercial biopharmaceutical company, the Director/Senior Director will help establish the people, processes, systems, governance, and external partnerships required for commercial pharmacovigilance.

The successful candidate will combine strong scientific and medical judgment with practical operational experience implementing pharmacovigilance capabilities in a growing organization.

Key Responsibilities

Pharmacovigilance Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and execute the pharmacovigilance strategy supporting late-stage clinical development, regulatory approval, product launch, and post-marketing surveillance.
  • Establish a scalable PV operating model appropriate for the company's anticipated commercial footprint, product portfolio, geographic expansion, and partnership structure.
  • Serve as a senior safety leader and subject matter expert for pharmacovigilance matters across Clinical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Affairs, Quality, Commercial, Legal, and other functions.
  • Provide safety input into clinical development plans, regulatory submissions, labeling strategies, launch-readiness activities, medical information processes, and lifecycle management.
  • Represent Pharmacovigilance on cross-functional governance and product development teams.
  • For the Senior Director level, provide strategic leadership to executive management regarding emerging safety issues, benefit-risk considerations, regulatory risk, and organizational PV capabilities.

Commercial Launch Readiness

  • Lead PV readiness activities required to transition from a clinical-stage to commercial-stage pharmacovigilance organization.
  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive PV launch-readiness plan, including commercial adverse event intake, case processing, reconciliation, vendor interfaces, escalation pathways, reporting responsibilities, and business continuity.
  • Establish processes for adverse event and product complaint intake from Medical Affairs, Medical Information, Commercial, Market Access, patient support programs, digital channels, distributors, partners, and other potential sources.
  • Partner with Quality and Commercial functions to ensure appropriate identification, triage, reconciliation, and escalation of safety information associated with product complaints.
  • Establish PV requirements and training for employees, contractors, vendors, field-based personnel, and other groups who may receive adverse event information.
  • Ensure PV systems, procedures, resources, vendors, and governance structures are operational and inspection-ready prior to product launch.

Safety Surveillance & Benefit-Risk Management

  • Establish and oversee processes for signal detection, validation, prioritization, assessment, management, and documentation.
  • Lead cross-functional safety review or Safety Management Team meetings.
  • Provide strategic oversight of aggregate safety reports and periodic benefit-risk assessments, including applicable DSURs, PBRERs/PSURs, and other periodic reports.
  • Lead or contribute to Risk Management Plans and other risk minimization activities.
  • Partner with Regulatory Affairs and Clinical Development on safety-related labeling changes, investigator communications, regulatory responses, and health authority interactions.

Pharmacovigilance Operations

  • Provide strategic and operational oversight of adverse event case management across clinical and post-marketing sources.
  • Ensure appropriate collection, assessment, processing, follow-up, quality review, and submission of ICSRs within applicable regulatory timelines.
  • Oversee PV vendors, including safety database providers, case-processing vendors, medical review resources, literature surveillance providers, and aggregate reporting partners.
  • Establish meaningful operational metrics, quality indicators, and vendor performance measures to monitor the effectiveness of the PV system.
  • Develop internal capabilities versus outsourced capabilities based on company growth, volume, geographic footprint, and portfolio requirements.
  • Ensure effective reconciliation of safety information across clinical databases, medical information, quality/product complaints, partners, patient support programs, and other relevant systems.

PV Quality, Compliance & Inspection Readiness

  • Partner closely with Quality Assurance to establish and maintain the company's pharmacovigilance quality system.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain PV policies, SOPs, work instructions, and controlled processes.
  • Establish appropriate deviation, CAPA, quality-event, and compliance-monitoring processes related to pharmacovigilance.
  • Maintain continuous PV inspection readiness and participate in regulatory authority inspections, partner audits, vendor audits, and internal audits.
  • Ensure documentation demonstrates effective oversight of outsourced PV activities.
  • Support development and maintenance of applicable PV system documentation and regulatory requirements, including the Pharmacovigilance System Master File (PSMF) where required.

Partnerships & Alliance Management

  • Develop and maintain Safety Data Exchange Agreements (SDEAs) and pharmacovigilance provisions within licensing, distribution, co-development, and commercialization agreements.
  • Establish clear responsibilities for case exchange, aggregate reporting, signal management, regulatory submissions, reconciliation, and safety governance.
  • Represent the company on joint safety committees and other alliance governance forums.
  • Monitor partner compliance with contractual PV obligations and implement corrective actions as necessary.

Regulatory Compliance

  • Maintain current knowledge of applicable global pharmacovigilance regulations and guidance, including requirements of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency (EMA), ICH, and other relevant health authorities.
  • Ensure company PV processes remain compliant as products transition from investigational to marketed status and expand geographically.
  • Support preparation for health authority meetings and responses to regulatory questions regarding product safety and benefit-risk.

Qualifications

Education

  • Advanced degree in a health or life sciences discipline strongly preferred, such as MD, PharmD, PhD, RN/NP, or equivalent scientific/medical training.
  • Candidates with a master's or bachelor's degree and significant relevant pharmacovigilance leadership experience may also be considered.

Experience

Director:

  • Typically 10+ years of pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry experience, including approximately 7+ years in pharmacovigilance/drug safety.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting late-stage clinical development and/or marketed products.
  • Experience managing outsourced PV operations and vendors.
  • Previous experience with NDA/BLA/MAA preparation, product launch, or post-marketing pharmacovigilance strongly preferred.

Senior Director:

  • Typically 12-15+ years of pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry experience with substantial progressive leadership responsibility within pharmacovigilance.
  • Demonstrated leadership of PV activities through late-stage development, regulatory approval, and commercial launch.
  • Experience establishing or significantly scaling a pharmacovigilance function, ideally within a small or mid-sized biotechnology company.
  • Experience interacting with senior executives, health authorities, strategic partners, and regulatory inspectors.

Technical Expertise

Strong working knowledge of:

  • Global pharmacovigilance regulations and regulatory reporting requirements
  • ICSR management and expedited reporting
  • Signal detection and signal management
  • Aggregate safety reporting
  • Benefit-risk assessment
  • Risk management planning and risk minimization
  • Safety governance
  • Safety database and PV technology environments
  • SDEAs and partner pharmacovigilance oversight
  • Vendor governance and outsourced PV models
  • PV quality systems, CAPAs, audits, and inspection readiness
  • Clinical-to-commercial PV transition

Experience with commercial safety systems such as Oracle Argus Safety or equivalent validated safety database platforms is desirable.

Leadership Competencies

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Builder mentality: Comfortable establishing infrastructure rather than inheriting a fully mature PV organization.
  • Strategic judgment: Ability to distinguish immediate launch-critical requirements from capabilities that can scale after commercialization.
  • Scientific rigor: Strong ability to interpret complex clinical and post-marketing safety information and translate it into actionable benefit-risk assessments.
  • Operational discipline: Ability to establish processes, governance, controls, metrics, and vendor accountability.
  • Cross-functional influence: Ability to work effectively with Clinical, Regulatory, Medical Affairs, Quality, Commercial, Legal, and executive leadership.
  • Risk-based decision making: Ability to identify material patient-safety and compliance risks and implement pragmatic solutions in a resource-conscious biotechnology environment.
  • Executive communication: Ability to communicate complex safety issues clearly and concisely to senior leadership and governance committees.
  • Hands-on leadership: Willingness to operate both strategically and tactically in a growing organization.

Preferred Experience

Particularly attractive candidates will have experience with several of the following:

  • First commercial product launch
  • Transition from clinical-stage to commercial-stage biotechnology
  • NDA or BLA submission and approval
  • U.S. and European product launches
  • Building or scaling an outsourced/hybrid PV operating model
  • Establishing post-marketing signal detection processes
  • Implementing or migrating a validated safety database
  • PSMF development and maintenance
  • FDA or European health authority PV inspections
  • Rare disease, oncology, specialty pharmaceutical, biologic, or other relevant therapeutic-area experience
  • Patient support programs and specialty pharmacy safety reporting
  • Commercial product complaint/adverse event reconciliation
  • Licensing, co-development, or co-commercialization partnerships

Rezolute (RZLT) currently anticipates the base salary for the Director / Senior Director, Pharmacovigilance Operations role could range from $255,000 to $315,000 and will depend in part on the successful candidate’s geographical location and their qualifications for the role, including education and experience. This position will also be eligible for an annual performance bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan (depending, in part, on company and individual performance and at the Company’s discretion on an individual basis). The compensation described above is subject to change and could be higher or lower than the range described based on current market survey data and the qualifications, education, experience, and geographical location of the selected candidate.

 

Qualifying employees are eligible to participate in benefit programs such as:

jobs.description_html:
ABOUT THE ROLE:

Our PBM goal is to help clients better manage pharmacy spend to make drugs more affordable for their employees and dependents. Rightway is responsible for designing, building, and operating a new-to-the-world PBM model based on our core tenets: fairness & transparency, unlocking the supply chain, supporting the physician-patient relationship, and utilizing navigation to empower consumers.

The Clinical Pharmacist, Specialty is a member of the Rightway PBM Clinical Operations team. This role will be key in delivering on the “pharmacist in the family” approach to engaging our members on specialty medications. We are looking for an experienced clinical pharmacist with specialty drug experience to engage with our specialty members in a caring and empathetic manner. Written and verbal communication skills will be critical when interacting with members on the phone, via email, and via the chat function on the Rightway app. A willingness to go the extra mile to provide outstanding customer service is an essential requirement of this role.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Guide specialty members as if you are the “Pharmacist in the Family” to help specialty members manage their medications and disease states. 
  • Engage with specialty members via phone, chat, and email to provide a white glove/concierge experience for members.
  • Support and assist specialty members in enrolling in copay/patient assistance programs. 
  • Onboard new specialty members: assist in drug selection (as needed), specialty clinical assessment, selection of a specialty dispensing pharmacy, clinically support member throughout the continuum of care. 
  • Go above and beyond to answer member questions about all things pharmacy related. 
  • Perform core Pharmacist duties including prospective/retrospective drug utilization reviews, comprehensive medication reviews, and recommending changes to patient's drug regimens. 
  • Partners with Rightway’s Navigation team where needed to provide holistic support to members. 
  • Contributes to the Pharmacy & Therapeutics process in the research, preparation and presentation of drug monographs, therapeutic category reviews and clinical policy development.
  • Ensures that these processes meet or exceed regulatory and best practice standards.
  • Supports prior authorization review process as needed regarding specialty drug product selection and formulary compliance to ensure quality of care. 
  • Effectively collaborate with third-parties in the administration of Rightway’s clinical pharmacy strategy.

WHO YOU ARE:

  • Core operating hours are weekdays within 8 am Eastern Time and 8 pm Pacific Time, but may be required to work an evening or weekend shift in the future as Rightway grows. On call approximately once every two months.
